name: baseline office policy
description: A small starter pack for a shared office network. Every pattern here is a defensive signature: it describes something worth noticing in a log, and nothing here performs any action against any host.

rules.label: Nightly backup job
rules.description: The scheduled backup account logging in on purpose. Allowed so it stops competing with the privilege rules below.

rules.label: Admin box on the office VLAN
rules.description: Key based login by the office admin account. Keys are the policy here, so this is what good looks like.

rules.label: Repeated SSH password failures
rules.description: Five or more failed SSH passwords from one address inside a short window. One failure is a typo. Five is somebody working through a list.

rules.label: Login attempt for an account that does not exist
rules.description: Somebody guessing account names. Worth seeing even once, because a real person knows their own username.

rules.label: Failed sudo attempt
rules.description: A failed privilege escalation on a shared box. Rare enough in normal use that each one deserves a look.

rules.label: Interactive root shell
rules.description: Somebody is working as root rather than through sudo. Usually a habit worth correcting, occasionally worth asking about.

rules.label: VPN certificate rejected
rules.description: A VPN client failing its handshake. Often an expired certificate, sometimes something else.

rules.label: Unexpected access point name
rules.description: The office access point reporting an SSID it does not recognise nearby. Low severity because coffee shops exist.

rules.label: Routine cron noise
rules.description: Cron opening and closing sessions all day. Ranked above the alert rules on purpose: a cron session for root is not somebody working as root, so this is the more specific rule and it should win. Tuning a noisy detection is what a rule like this is for.

rules.label: Monitoring health check
rules.description: The uptime checker doing its job once a minute.
